title: Marswalk sky view factor
description: Fraction of the upper hemisphere a crouching astronaut sees at each node of a 6 m grid over the terrain tile: 1 on open flat ground, lower where the terrain hides part of the sky. Less sky means less dose in a solar particle event, though far less than in proportion (see the provenance note). Read by the Exposure layer of the mission table and its route readout (src/sim/skyView.js). Built by scripts/build-sky-view.mjs; do not edit by hand.
frame: Node (0, 0) is the north-west corner of the tile, the last node the south-east corner; rows run south. x east, z south, metres from Cheyava Falls.
method: Ray cast on the 751 x 751 height grid, kept on every 3rd node: 48 azimuths, rays to 400 m or the tile edge, dose point 1 m above the ground. Visible fraction = mean over azimuths of (1 - sin(horizon elevation)), horizon clamped at 0. Same rays as public/data/shelters.json.
label: HiRISE DTM · sky view

provenance.site: Jezero crater, Neretva Vallis, around Cheyava Falls
provenance.reference: Marswalk terrain tile public/marswalk/assets/terrain.json (751 x 751 heights, 2 m spacing, from the HiRISE 1 m DEM of Jezero crater); sky view computed by src/sim/skyView.js through scripts/build-sky-view.mjs
provenance.locator: docs/route/shelters.md, sections "Why the terrain helps at all" and "Limits of the estimate"
provenance.license: HiRISE products are NASA/JPL/University of Arizona, public with no restriction of use (NASA SPD-41A).
provenance.note: The sky view is DERIVED geometry. Taking the dose on a route as its mean sky view times the open-ground dose assumes an isotropic SEP flux above the horizon, our assumption (SIM). The real flux is stronger toward the zenith, so hiding the low sky saves less: read 1 - sky view as an upper bound on the saving. The one measurement on Mars found a far smaller cut: Curiosity's RAD beside Butte M12, with 19 % of the sky blocked, measured about 4 % less dose (Ehresmann et al. 2021, JGR Planets 126, doi 10.1029/2021JE006851). Rays stop at the tile edge, which raises the sky view near the edge. On this 6 m grid the values span only 0.82 to 1; the full 2 m grid reaches 0.807 at its lowest node (public/data/shelters.json, sky_view.tile_stats), so the terrain never hides more than about 19 % of the sky.
